# Commands

<!-- Generated by `go generate .` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command is `lazyaria <command> [args]`. Flags may come before
or after the other arguments, and take one or two dashes (`-wait` and
`--wait` are the same). A job is named by its number, `14` or
`#14` as `lazyaria list` shows it, or by the first characters of its
ID, as long as they match only one job. Numbers are never reused.

Commands that talk to the daemon start it when it is not running. See
[The daemon](../concepts/the-daemon.md).

## Overview

This is what `lazyaria help` prints:

```text
usage: lazyaria <command> [args]
       lazyaria    open the terminal interface (in a terminal)
       lazyaria <link|magnet|file.torrent|->...
                   same as lazyaria add

commands:
  add [--dir D] [--out F] [--paused] [--wait] [--force] <link|file.torrent|->...
            queue downloads; - reads links from stdin; --wait exits 0
            when all finish, 1 if any fails; --force downloads a link
            that is already in the list
  list [--json] [--all] [--limit N]
            show jobs; --all includes finished ones; --limit shows
            at most N
  show [--json] <job>
            one job: files, sources, piece map and history
  status [--json]
            daemon and engine status
  pause|resume <job>...
            a job is its number (14 or #14) or the start of its id
  remove [--delete-files] <job>...
            prints an undo command that works for remove.undo_seconds
  undo <token>
            bring back what a remove took, files included
  refresh <job> <link>
            give a download a fresh link; it keeps its progress and
            its name
  config list [--json] | get KEY | set KEY VALUE | reset KEY | edit | path | keys
  doctor [--json] [--restart-engine]
            check the setup and say how to fix what is wrong
  logs [-f]  show the daemon log; -f keeps following it
  service install|uninstall
            run the daemon as a systemd user service
  daemon [--detach] [--mode on-demand|always]
            run the daemon (normally started automatically)
  version   print the version and IPC protocol
  help      show this help

exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 daemon unreachable, 4 duplicate or refused
```

## add

```text
add [--dir D] [--out F] [--paused] [--wait] [--force] <link|file.torrent|->...
          queue downloads; - reads links from stdin; --wait exits 0
          when all finish, 1 if any fails; --force downloads a link
          that is already in the list
```

Flags:

```text
  -dir string
    	download directory
  -force
    	add even if the link is already in the list
  -out string
    	file name to save as
  -paused
    	add the jobs paused
  -wait
    	wait until every job finishes; exit 1 if any fails
```

## config

```text
config list [--json] | get KEY | set KEY VALUE | reset KEY | edit | path | keys
```

## daemon

```text
daemon [--detach] [--mode on-demand|always]
          run the daemon (normally started automatically)
```

Flags:

```text
  -detach
    	run in the background and return once the daemon is up
  -mode string
    	on-demand or always (overrides daemon.mode)
```

## doctor

```text
doctor [--json] [--restart-engine]
          check the setup and say how to fix what is wrong
```

Flags:

```text
  -json
    	print JSON
  -restart-engine
    	restart aria2 with a freshly read config first
```

## help

```text
help      show this help
```

## list

```text
list [--json] [--all] [--limit N]
          show jobs; --all includes finished ones; --limit shows
          at most N
```

Flags:

```text
  -all
    	include finished jobs
  -json
    	print JSON
  -limit int
    	show at most N jobs (0 = all)
```

## logs

```text
logs [-f]  show the daemon log; -f keeps following it
```

Flags:

```text
  -f	keep printing new lines
```

```text

```

```text

```
